title: Coffee and coconut milk cold-process soap
subtitle: A creamy, mildly exfoliating bar with an espresso tone
excerpt: A cold-process soap bar with frozen coconut milk replacing the water in the lye solution, and fine coffee grounds stirred through the batter for a mild exfoliating texture. The coconut milk adds a creamier lather and a darker, warm-toned bar. Makes 7 bars.
sourceNotes: Coconut milk in cold-process soap (milk soaps): Susan Miller Cavitch, The Soapmaker's Companion (1997), chapter on milk soaps. Coffee grounds as soap additive: open-access soapmaking reference. Frozen milk lye technique to prevent scorching: standard milk-soap practice, documented across the soapmaking literature. SAP values and lye calculation from SoapCalc table.

recipe.batchNotes: Run any scale change through a lye calculator before batching. Keep milk usage at 33% of oil weight.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Freeze the coconut milk the day before. Allow 4 to 6 weeks cure.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years in a cool, dark cupboard once cured. Milk soaps have a slightly shorter shelf life than water-based soaps due to the fats in the milk. Discard if DOS (orange or brown spots) appear or the bar smells rancid.

glossaryTerms.definition: The chemical reaction between fat and sodium hydroxide that produces soap and glycerine. Each oil has a SAP value: the grams of lye needed to fully saponify one gram of that oil.

Cold-process soap in which some or all of the water is replaced with a milk or plant milk. Adding lye to milk at room temperature scorches the sugars; frozen milk prevents the temperature rising too fast and keeps the batch from turning orange.
The point at which the soap batter has thickened to thin-custard consistency. A drizzle holds briefly on the surface. The signal to pour.

projectSchedule.title: Unmould and cut
projectSchedule.body: Turn out the loaf. The bar will be a warm caramel-brown from the milk sugars. Cut wearing protective gloves. The colour deepens slightly over the cure period.

projectSchedule.title: Turn the bars
projectSchedule.body: Flip each bar for even curing. The coffee grounds should be evenly distributed through the cut face.

projectSchedule.title: Four-week test
projectSchedule.body: The bar is safe and ready to use at four weeks. The lather is creamy; the coffee grounds exfoliate lightly.

projectSchedule.title: Cure complete
projectSchedule.body: A fully cured milk-and-coffee bar is firm and dark. The scent is faintly of coffee; the lather is luxurious and creamy.

content.text: A
milk soap
made with frozen coconut milk instead of water, with fine coffee grounds stirred through the batter at
trace
. The
saponification

of the oil blend proceeds the same as a standard batch. The coconut milk produces a creamier lather and a naturally tanned bar colour. The coffee grounds add a fine exfoliating texture. Adding lye to frozen milk prevents the lactose scorching.
Freeze the coconut milk at least 24 hours before making. Put on protective gloves and goggles before handling lye.
Ingredients

items.prepNote: calculated at 5% superfat for this oil blend
full-fat coconut milk, frozen in cubes the day before; 33% of oil weight
fine or medium grind; stirred in at trace

content.text: Method
Make the lye solution on frozen milk

Place the frozen coconut-milk cubes in the HDPE lye pitcher in a bowl of ice. Working in a ventilated space with protective gloves and goggles on, add the sodium hydroxide to the frozen milk in a slow steady stream, stirring constantly. The lye dissolves the milk as the ice thaws; the ice prevents the temperature rising high enough to scorch the sugars. The mixture may turn orange at first; this lightens as it cools. Stir until fully dissolved and cool to 38 to 42°C.
Prepare the oils
Melt the coconut oil and shea butter together. Add the olive oil and castor oil. Cool to 38 to 42°C.
Blend to trace and add coffee

Pour the milk-lye solution into the oils. Blend with the stick blender to light trace. Stir in the ground coffee by hand until evenly distributed. Pour immediately into the mould; the coffee causes the batter to reach medium trace quickly.
Insulate, unmould, and cure
Wrap in a towel. Leave 48 hours. Unmould wearing protective gloves. Cut into bars. Cure on a rack for 4 to 6 weeks.
Storage and shelf life
Two years in a cool, dark cupboard on an open rack. Milk soaps are slightly more prone to rancidity than water-based soaps; store away from heat. Discard if DOS or a rancid smell develop.
